question.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 2 & 1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}],\,B=\{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c\end{aligned}]\}
$$

Consider the subspace $\text{Col}(A)$ and an orthogonal basis $B$ of $\text{Col}(A),$ where $A$ and $B$ are given above. Given that $B$ is derived from $\text{Col}(A)$ using the Gram-Schmidt process, what is the value of $\frac{a}{b}?$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that $\text{Col}(A)$ is the span of the columns of $A.$ 

First, let's denote

$\,$ ${a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$ 

We proceed to find an orthogonal basis using the Gram-Schmidt process, as follows.

**Step 1**: We set ${v}_{1}={a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}].$

**Step 2**: Next, we find ${v}_{2}$, by using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{2} & ={a}_{2}-\frac{{a}_{2}\cdot {v}_{1}}{{v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{1}}{v}_{1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the formula for ${v}_{2}$ in our case gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{2} & ={a}_{2}-\frac{2\cdot 1+1\cdot 2+2\cdot (-1)}{{1}^{2}+{2}^{2}+(-1)^{2}}{v}_{1} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]-\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{3} \\ \frac{1}{3} \\ \frac{7}{3}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $B=\{{v}_{1},{v}_{2}\}=\{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{3} \\ \frac{1}{3} \\ \frac{7}{3}\end{aligned}]\}$ is an orthogonal basis for $\text{Col}(A).$

Finally, $a=\frac{5}{3},$ $b=\frac{1}{3},$ and  

$$
\frac{a}{b}=\frac{(\frac{5}{3})}{(\frac{1}{3})}=5.
$$
